main_text.p: omnis doctrina est ex prœcognitis. Hinc vitemus sine prolegomenis artium & scientiarum tractationem non auspicari Philosophos, qui aliquam accurationis laudem sibi vendicant.

Unde egregij duo Zabarellæ libri nati, vnus de natura logicæ, alter de constitutione scientiæ physicæ. Eodem modo & reliqui Aristotelis Interpretes commentationibus suis logicis Physicis & metaphysicis proœmium seu prolegomena præmiserunt: quos inter laudo Toletum, Fonsecam, Pererium, Patres Conimbricenses & Fortunatum Crellium.
Proœmio quinque capita destinamus (1) de definitione Physicæ. (2) de causis. (3) de subjecto. (4) de cognatis. (5) de partitione.
Hæc fere sunt quæstiones de quibus plerique in scientiarum proœmiis disputare solent: videantur Zabarella, Toletus, Fonseca, Patres Conimbricenses, Pererius & alij.
main_text.head: Definitio est nominis vel rei.
main_text.p: Nomen si spectes, Physica est cognitio naturæ, quæ alias quoque appellatur physiologia, quæ est λόγος περὶ τῆς φύσεως: hoc est, sermo de natura, vel discursus de rebus naturalibus.

page.notes: Handwritten annotations were left out: "Proœmiorum capita" in the left margin, "Physices definitio" and "Nominalis" with the numeral "1" in the left margin, and the Greek marks "Ἐπιχρεσις" (or similar) before "Haec fere" and at the foot of the right side. The Greek at the end of the first column is printed text, not handwriting. The "II." and "III." are printed bare numerals and are rendered as paragraphs per the rules. The word "vitemus" has a pen mark over it; the reading is best judgement.
